items.originalTitle: ‘I’ll put a pillow under his butt’ – How Toto Wolff wants to solve Kimi Antonelli’s track limits problem
detailZh: “我在他屁股下面放个枕头”——托托·沃尔夫想如何解决基米·安东内利的赛道限制问题
安东内利一直难以遵守赛道限制，但梅赛德斯车队老板沃尔夫有一个解决的办法
梅赛德斯一级方程式车队负责人托托·沃尔夫在新加坡大奖赛上开玩笑说，基米·安东内利需要“在屁股下面放个枕头”才能更好地看到赛道上的白线
在滨海湾赛道比赛中，安东内利四次越过了赛道限制；第四次违规的理论惩罚是五秒罚时，但他因为其中一次是由于刹车问题导致失控而逃脱了惩罚。
这样的处罚并没有让车手积分榜领跑者损失任何东西——他以16秒的领先优势排在第三位，领先兰多·诺里斯——但这个危险仍然让沃尔夫感到有些不安。
当Motorsport.com问及，鉴于安东内利最近用不那么占优势的银箭赛车限制损失，我们是否看到了他进步的不同阶段时，沃尔夫承认：“我认为这是一个好的阶段，因为正如你所说，我们在一开始有一段时间赛车表现非常出色，他从中受益最大。
“但后来我们在吉隆坡赛道上推出了一辆不那么容易驾驶、速度较慢的赛车，我认为周末两位车手的工作使得今天的赛车表现并不差。
“它是否像应该的那样快？升级后并不快。但我认为他管理了自己的比赛，保持了冷静——除了几个超车线限制，我有一个很好的策略，我打算在他的屁股下面放一个酒店里的枕头，这样他实际上可以看到道路。因为我认为他看不到道路。
“这让我们感到压力。比赛的一半时间我们已经有三次违规，但也显示了他正在大量挑战极限。”
“我认为他驾驶的方式很成熟，很好。我们讨论了这件事，他说，‘我必须保持冷静，确保我完成比赛’。所以，在那个阶段处理一辆困难的赛车，并试图发展和学习，这是很好的。”
在第32圈时，安东内利报告说“我感觉到我的脚之间有东西在漏”，这短暂地引发了可靠性担忧，但梅赛德斯在数据中并没有发现任何异常。”
在比赛结束后不久接受媒体采访时，沃尔夫并没有得到任何线索。
“这个液体，我们不知道，”奥地利人说道。 “我们怀疑是那个饮料瓶出了问题，或者他有泄漏，但他应该知道如果是这样的话。”
然而，对于安东内利抱怨他的刹车踏板“太长”以至于“没有刹车”的解释是……
“另外一件事是他在刹车中出现了热衰减，我认为是在停车后，这就是为什么踏板变长，然后在他得到更多空气冷却后立即恢复，”沃尔夫详细解释道。
安东内利的领奖台成绩，加上乔治·拉塞尔最新的挫折，意味着这位年轻人下周在美国大奖赛上赢得世界冠军的机会虽然渺茫。
detailEn: ‘I’ll put a pillow under his butt’ – How Toto Wolff wants to solve Kimi Antonelli’s track limits problem
Antonelli has been struggling to stick to track limits, but Mercedes team boss Wolff has an idea how to solve it
Mercedes Formula 1 team principal Toto Wolff has joked Kimi Antonelli needs “a pillow under his butt” to better see the white lines on track, following the Singapore Grand Prix.

In the Marina Bay race, Antonelli breached track limits on four occasions; the theoretical punishment for a fourth strike is a five-second penalty, but he escaped it given one of those was down to a loss of control amid brake issues.

Such a sanction wouldn’t have cost the championship leader anything – he finished third with a comfortable 16-second gap to Lando Norris – but the jeopardy still left Wolff a little too uneasy to his taste.

Asked by Motorsport.com if we were seeing a different phase in Antonelli’s progress, given the Italian has been limiting the damage with a less dominant Silver Arrow lately, Wolff acknowledged: “I think it's a good phase because, exactly like you say, we had a car that was dominant for long spells at the beginning, and he did the best out of it.

“But then we put a car on the track in Kuala Lumpur that wasn't easy, that was slower, and I think the work over the weekend from the two drivers led to a point that the car in the race today was not bad.

“Was it as quick as it should have been? With the upgrade, it wasn't. But I think he managed his race, he kept his cool – other than a few of the track limits, where I have a good strategy, I'm going to put a pillow from the hotel under his butt, so he can actually see the road. Because I think he can't see it.
“That stresses us. Half the race we already have three strikes, but it also shows that he's pushing the limits a lot.

“I think how he's driven that is mature and good. We talked about it and he said, ‘I've just got to keep my calm here and make sure that I finish the race’. So, handling a difficult car at that stage and trying to develop it and learn, it's good.”
On lap 32, Antonelli reported “I feel something leaking between my feet”, briefly sparking reliability concerns, but Mercedes couldn’t see anything of note on the data.
When addressing the media moments after the race, Wolff was none the wiser.
“The liquid, we don't know,” the Austrian said. “We suspect it was the drink bottle that went there, or he had a leak, but he should have known that if it was the case.”
However, there was an explanation to Antonelli’s complaint about his brake pedal being “so long” that he had “no brakes”.

“The other thing is that he had a heat soak in the brakes, I think it was after the stop, and that is why the pedal went long and then recovered immediately after when he got more air cooling it again,” Wolff detailed.
Antonelli’s podium finish, on top of George Russell’s latest setback, means the youngster has an outside chance of clinching the world title at the United States Grand Prix next week.

观看新加坡大奖赛的开赛，马克斯·维斯塔潘成功抵挡住了查尔斯·勒克莱尔
“红牛车队表现不错。但我们不仅要与迈凯轮车队竞争，还要与梅赛德斯车队竞争，”他说。
“赛季初，梅赛德斯车队表现神勇，然后迈凯轮车队赢得了两到三场比赛，接着红牛车队赢得了两到三场比赛。”
“四支车队之间的差距不到两十分之一。如果有人带来升级，排名可能会改变。最重要的是专注于自己。”

detailEn: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver releases statement on Instagram after 'painful lesson' at Singapore GP

Lewis Hamilton took to social media to apologise to Ferrari once again after his strategy call saw him drop out of the podium positions at the Singapore Grand Prix; watch every session of the United States GP in Austin on October 23-25, live on Sky Sports F1
Sky Sports F1's Karun Chadhok dissects Lewis Hamilton's Singapore GP race
Lewis Hamilton has posted on social media to reiterate has apology to Ferrari after a "painful lesson" at the Singapore Grand Prix.

Hamilton overrode Ferrari's strategy while on course for a podium finish by opting not to pit for fresh tyres during a Virtual Safety Car (VSC) period, leaving him vulnerable in the closing stages of the race.

He was overtaken by Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc, who did pit when the VSC came out, and was subsequently passed by Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli, plus McLaren duo Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri as he dropped to sixth.

Hamilton was excused from fulfilling his media duties after the race as he felt unwell after competing in the sweltering conditions, but released a statement via Ferrari, and has posted himself on Instagram on Monday with similar comments.

"Yesterday wasn't the result we were looking for, and that's on me. At a track that's difficult to overtake, you need to try something different and I chose a strategy that ultimately didn't deliver," he wrote.
Lewis Hamilton apologised to his team for his strategy call in Singapore

"It's a painful lesson to learn, but I take full responsibility for the decisions I made. In this sport, not every call will work out. It's about accepting when you get it wrong and how you move forward.
"I'm grateful to the team for the work they put in every weekend. P6 doesn't reflect the pace we had in the car over the weekend, and despite the result there are positives to take away.
"Massive thanks to the fans in Singapore for the energy. I'll continue to put the work in and come back fighting at the next race."
Highlights from the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix
Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur was asked several questions about Hamilton's decision and was eager to stress to not put any blame on the team.
"It was clearly a mistake when you see the outcome, it was not a good call," said Vasseur.

"But, on the other hand, quite often you have to listen to the drivers because they are in the car and have the feeling with the tyres but for this one it is clear for me. But I respect their feeling in the car."
Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur confirms Lewis Hamilton was supposed to pit under the Virtual Safety Car, but stayed out

Ferrari were hoping to challenge Max Verstappen for victory in Singapore but they closest they came was at the start when Leclerc almost drew alongside the Red Bull driver but was forced to back out going into Turn 1.
Leclerc put Verstappen under pressure during the early stages of the race before fading away and finished seven seconds behind the Dutchman.
Vasseur pointed out Ferrari "struggled more" compared to Red Bull in traffic but admits F1's top four teams are very close on pace.
Watch the start of the Singapore Grand Prix where Max Verstappen fended off Charles Leclerc
"Red Bull are doing well. But we have to fight with McLaren and Mercedes [as well]," he said.
"At the beginning of the season Mercedes were flying, then McLaren won two or three [races], then Red Bull won two pr three [races].
"We have four teams in less than two tenths. If someone brings an upgrade, the classification can change. The most important is to focus on yourselves."

items.originalTitle: How Kimi Antonelli escaped a Singapore GP track limits penalty despite four violations
detailZh: 尽管有四次违规，基米·安东内利如何在新加坡大奖赛赛道限界处罚中逃脱
一个关于出站的技术性条款阻止了基米·安东内利在新加坡大奖赛中因国际汽联的处罚而失去领奖台
对于梅赛德斯车迷来说，这里是关于银箭的最新消息，包括来自布拉克利和布里克斯沃斯的F1新闻、车手更新、赛车发展和比赛分析
在2026年新加坡大奖赛的发车旗落下后，F1粉丝和赛道观察员在官方计时图形确认冠军领跑者安德烈亚·基米·安东内利在62圈比赛中累积了四次单独的赛道限界违规时，感到深深分歧。
根据国际汽联制定的处罚指南，在一场大奖赛中累积四次违规应该触发自动五秒时间处罚。如果这项处罚被应用于安东内利的比赛时间，他艰苦争得的第三名成绩将瞬间消失，使他落后于麦凯轮车队的兰多·诺里斯，严重复杂化了他进入美国大奖赛时的积分领先局势。
然而，当最终成绩公布时，安东内利仍然稳坐在领奖台上毫发无损。深入官方国际汽联文件和体育规则，可以确切地了解到为什么这位梅赛德斯车星逃脱了处罚——以及为什么这个决定引发了激烈的争论。
文件88中详细列出的四次违规
在滨海湾街道赛道的赛道限制监控主要集中在前2、7、16和19弯。根据国际汽联文件88，该文件由赛事裁判在当地时间22:53发布，安东内利被指控在四次不同场合离开了赛车道。
第一击：20小时33分44秒在弯道2（圈速：1分37.395秒）
第二击：20小时35分21秒在弯道2（圈速：1分37.605秒）
第三击：21小时1分39秒在弯道19（圈速：1分37.221秒）
第四击：21小时9分33秒在弯道7（圈速：出站圈）
根据FIA一级方程式规则的附录L第四章第二条第2(c)款和第B1.8.6款，表面上似乎有四个条目符合时间处罚的门槛。追踪系统记录了针对车号12的四次红色违规标记，这立即激起了竞争对手粉丝基础的强烈不满，他们质疑冠军车手是否受到了特殊待遇。
安东内利逃脱的核心解释直接源于他在7号弯的第四次记录违规行为。
根据FIA的官方处罚指南，比赛中超车线有特定的解释："车手不能将时间设置在白色线条之外"。累积违规进程——第三次违规将获得黑白警告旗，第四次则触发五秒处罚——旨在惩罚车手在竞争性计时飞驰圈中反复获得微小优势的行为。
安东内利的第四次违规发生在21小时09分33秒，当时他正在进行维修区后的出站圈。由于他处于出站圈，没有在计时表上建立或记录任何竞争性圈速。根据国际体育法典第12.4.1.e条款的严格解释，文件88中发出的唯一命令是删除显示的圈速。
由于出站圈没有代表性的圈速可以从中扣除，并且因为7号弯道处没有在赛道外获得持续的体育优势或超越，裁判没有将此事件视为可能导致比赛中时间处罚的竞争性处罚。
程序上的失误：缺失的黑白色旗帜
在出站圈的技术性细节之外，一个次要的程序因素保护了安东内利免受赛后处罚：正式的警告结构。
根据FIA的标准操作协议，在为随后的第四次违规行为分配时间处罚之前，赛事控制必须正式向车手出示黑白色旗帜。在涉及安全车阶段、维修区窗口混乱和通过脏空气的激烈比赛中，安东内利从未在计时器上被正式显示黑白色警告。在没有触发赛事控制中规定的中间警告的情况下，立即发出五秒的赛后处罚将违反FIA自己的执法协议。
现在，安东内利虽然合法地保留了他在领奖台上的位置，但这一事件再次引发了对他驾驶精准度的审查。在整个2026赛季中，意大利人在赛道限制的遵守上一直是一个持续的挑战，由于他过于激进的弯道进入风格，导致几圈资格赛和比赛时段受到影响。
值得注意的是，如果安东内利在标准飞驰圈而不是出站圈时越过了7号弯的白线，那么5秒的降级是不可避免的。相反，这位年轻的梅赛德斯车手带着102分的积分优势前往奥斯汀，尽管整个车队的维修区都在更加密切地关注他的赛车位置。
detailEn: How Kimi Antonelli escaped a Singapore GP track limits penalty despite four violations
How a technicality on an out-lap prevented Kimi Antonelli from losing his Singapore GP podium to an FIA penalty
For Mercedes fans. All the latest from the Silver Arrows, with F1 news, driver updates, car development and race analysis from Brackley and Brixworth.

Following the chequered flag at the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix, Formula 1 fans and paddock observers were left deeply divided when official timing graphics confirmed that championship leader Andrea Kimi Antonelli had accumulated four separate track limit violations during the 62-lap race.

Under the FIA’s established penalty guidelines, reaching four strikes in a grand prix is supposed to trigger an automatic five-second time penalty. Had that sanction been applied to Antonelli's race time, his hard-fought third-place finish would have instantly evaporated, demoting him behind McLaren's Lando Norris and severely complicating his championship lead heading into the United States Grand Prix.

Yet, when the final classification was published, Antonelli remained untouched on the podium. A deep dive into the official FIA documentation and the governing body’s sporting code reveals exactly why the Mercedes star escaped sanction - and why the decision has sparked fierce debate.
The four violations detailed in document 88

Track limit monitoring at the Marina Bay Street Circuit was focused primarily on Turns 2, 7, 16, and 19. According to FIA Document 88, published by the race stewards at 22:53 local time, Antonelli was cited for leaving the racing surface on four distinct occasions:
Strike one: Turn 2 at 20h33m44s (Lap time: 1m37.395s)
Strike two: Turn 2 at 20h35m21s (Lap time: 1m37.605s)
Strike three: Turn 19 at 21h01m39s (Lap time: 1m37.221s)
Strike four: Turn 7 at 21h09m33s (Lap time: Out-lap)

On paper, four entries under Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2(c) and Article B1.8.6 of the FIA Formula 1 Regulations appeared to meet the threshold for a time penalty. The tracking system recorded four red violation markers against car number 12, triggering immediate outrage among rival fan bases that questioned whether the championship leader was receiving preferential treatment.
The core explanation behind Antonelli’s escape lies directly in the nature of his fourth recorded infraction at Turn 7.

According to the FIA’s official Penalty Guidelines, track limits during a race carry a specific clarification: "a driver cannot set a time outside the white lines". The cumulative strike progression - where the third offence earns a black-and-white warning flag and the fourth triggers a five-second penalty - is designed to punish drivers for repeatedly gaining a micro-advantage on competitive, timed flying laps.

Antonelli’s fourth breach at 21h09m33s occurred on an out-lap immediately following a pitstop. Because he was on an out-lap, no competitive lap time was being established or logged on the timing sheets. Under the strict interpretation of Article 12.4.1.e of the International Sporting Code, the only mandate issued in Document 88 was the deletion of the lap times shown.

Since an out-lap has no representative lap time to strike from the record, and because no lasting sporting advantage or overtake was gained off track at Turn 7, the stewards did not treat the incident as a competitive strike that would escalate to an in-race time penalty.
The procedural breakdown: The missing black-and-white flag
Beyond the out-lap technicality, a secondary procedural factor protected Antonelli from a post-race penalty: the formal warning structure.

Under standard FIA operational protocol, race control must formally display a black-and-white flag to a driver upon their third track limit violation before a time penalty can be assigned for a subsequent fourth breach. Amid a frantic mid-race phase involving safety car periods, pit-window scrambles, and battles through dirty air, Antonelli was never officially shown the black-and-white warning on the timing monitors. Without that mandated intermediary warning being triggered in race control, issuing an immediate five-second post-race penalty would have breached the FIA’s own enforcement protocol.

Now, while Antonelli legally retained his podium, the incident has reignited scrutiny over his driving precision. Track limit compliance has been an ongoing struggle for the Italian across the 2026 season, with several qualifying laps and race stints compromised by his aggressive corner-entry style.

It is important to note that had Antonelli crossed the white lines at Turn 7 on a standard flying lap rather than an out-lap, the five-second demotion would have been unavoidable. Instead, the young Mercedes driver heads to Austin with his 102-point championship cushion intact - though with the entire paddock watching his car placement far more closely.

FIA的处罚指南在此次事件中引发争议。

items.originalTitle: Kimi Antonelli’s title hopes boosted by proposed F1 calendar overhaul
detailZh: 基米·安东内利的车手冠军希望因拟议中的F1赛历大改而增强
中东地区日益加剧的安全威胁迫使F1将卡塔尔和阿布扎比大奖赛替换为伊莫拉决赛
对于梅赛德斯车迷来说，这里是关于银箭的最新消息，包括来自布拉克利和布里克斯沃思的F1新闻、车手更新、赛车发展和比赛分析
2026年F1世界锦标赛的最后阶段正面临一次巨大且前所未有的后勤大改。在中东地区安全局势急剧升级——特别是今天利雅得机场连续发生爆炸事件的报道——之后，体育管理机构正迅速采取措施取消赛季结束时的卡塔尔和阿布扎比大奖赛。
虽然一级方程式CEO斯蒂法诺·多米尼卡利之前表示希望在本赛季结束于中东，但不可预测的地缘政治气候迫使商业权益持有者激活了极端的欧洲应急计划。
原计划在亚斯码头赛道结束2026赛季的一级方程式，现在正在准备在恩佐·费拉利赛道宣布世界冠军。
查尔斯·勒克莱尔、法拉利、刘易斯·汉密尔顿、法拉利、马克斯·维斯塔潘、红牛车队
伊莫拉已经准备了数月作为备用选项，包括临时看台的建造在内的准备工作已经在幕后悄然进行。如果中东赛段正式取消，伊莫拉计划于12月6日举办艾米利亚-罗马涅大奖赛，取代原本为阿布扎比赛季决赛预留的日期。
如果一级方程式执行这个赛历变更，对2026年世界车手锦标赛的影响将是巨大的。
根据最初的赛程，新加坡之后还有六场大奖赛，最多还有150个积分。然而，用伊莫拉的单场赛事周末替换卡塔尔和阿布扎比，将剩余的总积分池降至仅125个。
目前，梅赛德斯车手安德烈亚·基米·安东内利以340个积分领跑积分榜，领先队友乔治·拉塞尔102个积分，拉塞尔以238个积分排在第二位。由于积分上限正在积极缩水，安东内利将成为事实上的世界冠军。
如果由于赛历危机人为地缩短了冠军争夺战，安东内利的加冕几乎不可避免。
在没有可能发生灾难性的连续退赛的情况下，安东内利在美洲三站赛事——包括美国、墨西哥和巴西——之前，就能在车队回到欧洲之前从数学上淘汰掉其他车手。如果赛历正式缩短至剩余五场比赛，那么在奥斯汀的美国赛车场赢得胜利将无疑确保冠军头衔，打破历史上最年轻F1世界冠军的记录。
随着国际汽联继续监控中东地区不断恶化的安全形势，梅赛德斯车队前往德克萨斯州时知道，冠军奖杯实际上已经握在他们手中。
detailEn: Kimi Antonelli’s title hopes boosted by proposed F1 calendar overhaul
Escalating security threats in the Middle East are pushing F1 to replace the Qatar and Abu Dhabi GPs with an Imola finale
For Mercedes fans. All the latest from the Silver Arrows, with F1 news, driver updates, car development and race analysis from Brackley and Brixworth.

The final stretch of the 2026 Formula 1 World Championship is facing a massive, unprecedented logistical overhaul. Following severe security escalations across the Middle East - specifically punctuated by reports of consecutive bombings at Riyadh airport today - the sport's governing body is rapidly moving to scrap the season-ending Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix.

While Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali previously stated a desire to finish the season in the Middle East, the unpredictable geopolitical climate has forced the commercial rights holders to activate a drastic European contingency plan.
Instead of wrapping up the 2026 campaign at the Yas Marina Circuit, Formula 1 is preparing to crown its world champion at the Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari.
Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing

Imola has been kept on standby for months as a fail-safe option, with preparatory infrastructure work - including the construction of temporary grandstands - already quietly under way behind the scenes. If the Middle Eastern leg is officially cancelled, Imola is slated to host the Emilia-Romagna Grand Prix on 6 December, taking the date originally reserved for the Abu Dhabi season finale.
If Formula 1 executes this calendar change, the impact on the 2026 world drivers' championship is huge.

Under the original schedule, six grands prix remained after Singapore, leaving a maximum of 150 points on the table. However, replacing both Qatar and Abu Dhabi with a single-race weekend at Imola drops the total remaining points pool to just 125.

Currently, Mercedes driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli leads the standings with 340 points, holding a massive 102-point advantage over his team-mate George Russell, who sits in second with 238 points. Because the points ceiling is actively shrinking, Antonelli would be the de facto world champion.
If the title fight is artificially condensed by the calendar crisis, Antonelli’s coronation is practically inevitable.

Without, maybe, a catastrophic string of consecutive DNFs across the upcoming Americas triple-header - featuring the United States, Mexico, and Brazil - Antonelli will mathematically eliminate the rest of the grid long before the paddock returns to Europe. If the calendar is officially shortened to five remaining races, a victory at the Circuit of the Americas in Austin would definitively secure the championship, obliterating the record for the youngest F1 world champion in history.
As the FIA continues to monitor the deteriorating safety situation in the Middle East, the Mercedes garage heads to Texas knowing the championship trophy is essentially already in their hands.

detailZh: 梅赛德斯确认，在新加坡大奖赛采用分策略后，基米·安东内利的升级方案“明显更快”
在新加坡大奖赛中采用分策略后，梅赛德斯终于为他们的F1升级方案找到了明确的发展路径
对于梅赛德斯车迷来说，这里是关于银箭的最新消息，包括来自布拉克利和布里克斯沃斯的F1新闻、车手更新、赛车发展和比赛分析
梅赛德斯F1车队在充满挑战的2026年新加坡大奖赛中不仅赢得了奖杯和稳定的车队积分，而且在整个周末都运行了一个分规格车库来评估他们备受争议的空气动力学升级方案，车队现在正式拥有了攻击赛季最后阶段所需的关键数据。
随着安东内利·基米·安东内利驾驶最新的开发套件，以及老将乔治·拉塞尔使用较旧的空气动力学规格，梅赛德斯在艰苦的滨海湾街道赛道上将其作为现场测试场地。
进入新加坡站，梅赛德斯维修区墙知道在冲刺周末赛制中找到他们修改后的W17的干净设置窗口将极其困难。然而，根据赛道工程总监安德鲁·肖夫林的说法，巨大的工程赌注最终得到了回报。
肖夫林在周日的检旗仪式后解释说：“本周末的主要目标之一是继续评估更新套件，并了解如何最大限度地发挥其作用。我们在三天的时间里学到了很多，更重要的是，一旦我们能够接近正确的操作窗口，我们在资格赛和比赛条件中都看到了令人鼓舞的迹象。”
乔治·拉塞尔，梅赛德斯，安东内利·基米·安东内利，梅赛德斯
虽然拉塞尔的赛车因为60个位置的网格处罚而严重受损，被迫从第19位起步，但他仍然设法将老款赛车强行开进积分区。与此同时，安东内利最大化了新的地板和翼片元素，管理轮胎磨损，确保了精彩的领奖台结束。
"基米驾驶了一场非常成熟的比赛，很好地管理了他的轮胎，然后有了速度来做出确保领奖台位置的动作，"肖夫林赞扬道。"乔治从后面起步的比赛一直都很具挑战性，但他一直努力战斗，做出了一些精彩的超越，并让自己回到了积分区。
经过几周努力平衡赛车的高速和低速特性，梅赛德斯终于对要追求的技术路径有了明确的答案。
"到周末结束时，基米的赛车明显比另一辆更快，这让我们有信心我们在开发方向上是正确的，"肖夫林确认。
安东内利在即将到来的美国大奖赛上，从数学角度上已经可以锁定2026年世界车手锦标赛的冠军，此时解锁升级套件的真正速度，对于布拉克利工厂来说再合适不过了。
"还有工作要做，但我们收集到的数据将对我们为奥斯汀做准备时非常有价值，"肖夫林总结道。"我们现在对性能在哪里以及我们需要关注什么以在赛季最后几场比赛中释放更多潜力有了更清晰的方向。"
detailEn: Mercedes confirms Kimi Antonelli’s upgrades are “clearly faster” after Singapore split strategy
After running split specifications in Singapore, Mercedes finally has a clear development path for their F1 upgrades
For Mercedes fans. All the latest from the Silver Arrows, with F1 news, driver updates, car development and race analysis from Brackley and Brixworth.

The Mercedes F1 Team walked away from the demanding 2026 Singapore Grand Prix with more than just a trophy and a solid haul of Constructors' points. After spending the entire weekend running a split-specification garage to evaluate their heavily debated aerodynamic updates, the team officially possesses the critical data needed to attack the final stretch of the season.

With Andrea Kimi Antonelli running the latest development package and veteran George Russell using an older aerodynamic specification, Mercedes used the grueling Marina Bay Street Circuit as a live testing ground.

Heading into Singapore, the Mercedes pitwall knew that finding a clean set-up window for their modified W17 would be incredibly difficult during a Sprint weekend format. However, according to Trackside Engineering Director Andrew Shovlin, the massive engineering gamble ultimately paid off.

"One of the main objectives this weekend was to continue our evaluation of the update package and build our understanding of how to get the most from it," Shovlin explained following Sunday's chequered flag. "We learned a lot over the three days and, importantly, saw encouraging signs in both qualifying and race conditions once we were able to move closer to the right operating window."
George Russell, Mercedes, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes

While Russell's race was severely compromised by a 60-place grid penalty that forced him to start 19th, he still managed to aggressively wrestle his older-spec car into the points. Meanwhile, Antonelli maximised the new floor and wing elements, managing his tyre degradation to secure a brilliant podium finish.

"Kimi drove a very mature race, managed his tyres well, and then had the pace to make the moves that secured the podium," Shovlin praised. "George’s race was always going to be challenging starting from the back, but he fought hard throughout, made some brilliant overtakes and got himself back into the points."
After weeks of struggling to balance the car's high-speed and low-speed characteristics, Mercedes finally has a definitive answer on which technical path to pursue.
"By the end of the weekend, Kimi’s package was clearly the faster of the two which gives us confidence that we are heading in the right direction from a development perspective," Shovlin confirmed.

With Antonelli mathematically positioned to potentially clinch the 2026 world drivers' championship at the upcoming United States Grand Prix, unlocking the true pace of the upgrade package could not have happened at a better time for the Brackley factory.

"There is still work to do, but the data we’ve gathered will be valuable as we prepare for Austin," Shovlin concluded. "We now have a clearer direction on where the performance is and what we need to focus on to unlock more of its potential over the final races of the season."

“我很高兴，兰多在某个阶段比赛中采取了这种思维方式。这就是作为车队经理我所期望的。这也是在麦克拉伦工作的1000多人期望我们的车手所做到的。”
“所以，我们有这个例子是好事，我肯定未来还会看到更多这样的情况，不管他们是在广播中被听到，还是在每个会议的闭门会议中发生，或者是在我们制定赛车计划的方式中。”
诺里斯对这一事件的公开反应随着周末的进行而发生了变化，最初在周六声称“这是一个很大的差距”，所以他“有权利”发起攻击。
然而，在周日的赛后，这位英国人承认他“本不应该尝试”超车，皮亚斯蒂补充说‘这本来就不需要发生’，但他已经从这件事中走出来了。
这使斯泰拉在麦凯轮车队为保持 constructors’ standings 第三名的位置而战斗时感到高兴，因为复苏的红牛车队在最后一轮的比赛中落后只有七分。
“我们昨天所发生的事情，我将其归类为不可接受，这是一个来自车队主管的声明，”斯特拉补充道。
“但我对这一点感到非常鼓舞，因为这也是我们的车手们迅速做出的声明。
兰多·诺里斯，麦克拉伦，奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里，麦克拉伦
“因此，我们在如何共同领导这个团队向前发展的问题上达成了共识，这是车队和车手们共同努力的结果。
“我们正在进行的对话还没有结束。但这并不是因为我们需要回去讨论Lando是否像以前那样和Oscar并排，那不是有趣的部分。”
“对我来说，有趣的部分是所有利益相关者、车队、车手必须围绕如何共同生活在这个团队中进行的反思。”
“始终从驾驶舱内部拥抱团队利益，将其视为高于任何特定个人利益的。”
detailEn: Andrea Stella praises Lando Norris for reaction to Singapore GP sprint clash
Norris collided into McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri on the last lap of the Singapore sprint race at Marina Bay
McLaren Formula 1 boss Andrea Stella has praised Lando Norris for the way he responded to his clash with team-mate Oscar Piastri in the Singapore Grand Prix sprint race.
The McLaren pair were squabbling over fourth on Saturday until Norris made an opportunistic lunge down the inside of Turn 5 during the final lap, causing both to collide at the apex.
It forced Piastri into a retirement with Norris dropping to eighth, though the reigning world champion avoided punishment as stewards claimed “both drivers had contributed”.

McLaren’s hierarchy was nevertheless furious, but spirits were higher on Sunday when Norris finished fourth and offered to help Piastri in his successful late attack on Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton for fifth.

“While the conversations from this point of view are not concluded, there's more we can do to become a more united and even stronger team,” said Stella, whose squad is now without a podium in three rounds.

“I'm pleased that Lando, at some stage in the race, adopted this way of thinking. This is what I expect as a team principal. This is what the 1,000 people that work at McLaren expect from our drivers.

“So, it's good that we have had this example and I expect definitely more of that in the future, independently of the fact that they will be heard on the radio or they will happen behind the closed door in every meeting or in the way we approach our race plan.”
The way Norris publicly reacted to the incident certainly changed as the weekend progressed, initially claiming on Saturday that “it was a big gap” so he had the “right” to attack.
Yet post-race on Sunday the Briton accepted that he “should never have attempted” the overtake, with Piastri adding it ‘didn’t need to happen’ but he’s already moved on from it.
This left Stella pleased amid McLaren’s fight to hold onto third in the constructors’ standings, as a resurgent Red Bull is just seven points behind after Max Verstappen won the last two rounds.
“What we had yesterday I classified it as unacceptable, which is a statement that comes from the team principal,” added Stella.
“But I was very encouraged by the fact that it's a statement that very rapidly came from our drivers as well.
Lando Norris, McLaren, Oscar Piastri, McLaren
“So, we are aligned as to how we want to lead this team forward in a joint effort between the team and the drivers.
“The conversations that we are having, they are not finished. But it's not because we need to go back discussing if Lando was alongside Oscar like with...that's not the interesting bit.
“For me, the interesting bit is a reflection that all the stakeholders, the team, the drivers will have to make around living together the team.
“Embracing constantly from inside the cockpit the interest of the team as something that is superior to any particular singular individual interest.”

items.originalTitle: McLaren boss Andrea Stella lays down the law after “unacceptable” F1 Sprint clash
detailZh: 麦凯轮负责人安德烈亚·斯特拉在新加坡大奖赛F1 Sprint碰撞后下达严令
安德烈亚·斯特拉在兰多·诺里斯和奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里在新加坡的Sprint赛事中发生不可接受的碰撞后要求团队团结
对于麦凯轮的粉丝来说，来自沃金克的最新消息，包括车手、赛车、团队策略以及每个周末的赛事。
2026年新加坡大奖赛为麦凯轮提供了严峻的现实检验。尽管兰多·诺里斯和奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里最终在周日的正赛中获得了双倍积分的完赛，但周六的Sprint赛事中的一场灾难性的团队内碰撞以及与锦标赛对手的明显速度差距严重影响了整个周末。
随着黑白旗的落下，麦凯轮车队负责人安德烈亚·斯特拉针对车辆当前的性能上限和内部车库动态进行了阐述，明确表示在车队为 车队的位置而战时，不会容忍自私的驾驶行为。
麦凯轮本周末的爆发点发生在雨中 短距离冲刺赛的最后一圈。在追击法拉利的查尔斯·勒克莱尔时，诺里斯在5号弯对帕斯蒂里进行了一次激进的内部切入。两辆 车队名称赛车发生了严重的碰撞，导致帕斯蒂里撞墙退赛，而诺里斯艰难地以第八名的成绩完赛，这使车队损失了大量 车队积分。
斯特拉立即召集了两位车手的会议，要求他们对赛车规则进行彻底的重置。
“至于昨天在 短距离冲刺赛中发生的事情，我说这是一个不可接受的事件，我很高兴我们的车手也持有这种观点，”斯特拉在周日的 大奖赛之后透露。“因此，我们在如何共同推动车队向前发展的问题上达成了共识。”
兰多·诺里斯，梅赛德斯，奥斯卡·皮亚斯蒂，梅赛德斯
而不是对5号弯道接触事件进行明确的责备，梅赛德斯车队经理利用这次灾难来强化车队的基本运营理念。
“我们将进一步讨论，但不是因为我们需要重新审视接触的‘为什么’或‘如何’，而是要一起反思我们想要成为什么样的团队，”斯特拉坚定地说。“我们必须意识到，无论我们是在工厂、维修区还是在汽车的驾驶舱中，车队利益高于任何个人的利益。”
诺里斯最终通过车队无线电为这次事件道歉，斯特拉希望这将成为未来的标准。
“这就是我从我和在迈凯伦 Mastercard工作的每个人那里期望我们的车手做到的，”斯泰拉补充道。“因此，我对兰多在比赛最后几圈所说的话感到很高兴，我期待在未来看到更多这样的例子。”
除了内部车库的政治斗争之外，斯泰拉公开承认，MCL40目前缺乏持续挑战红牛和法拉利赢得比赛胜利的原始空气动力学性能。
总的来说，今天的成绩反映了我们汽车当前的性能水平：它与我们在昨天排位赛中看到的情况非常相似，这并非巧合，”斯泰拉承认。“也许兰多有机会获得第三名，但在一个充满挑战的周六和几场比赛中我们没有取得我们希望的结果之后，获得这些积分是一种小小的安慰。”
奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里，迈凯伦，兰多·诺里斯，迈凯伦
然而，随着即将到来的关键的三连赛——包括在奥斯汀、墨西哥和巴西的比赛——斯特拉确认，沃金正在准备一个重大发展包来重燃本赛季的势头。
“这让我们在准备下一组三场比赛并专注于引入我们希望能够让我们争夺领奖台的更新时充满信心，”斯特拉总结道。“我们知道尽管红牛车队迈出了步伐，但这个结果证实了我们与锦标赛中当前的主要竞争对手正处在激烈的竞争中，而且我们认为我们能够缩小与领跑者的差距。”
detailEn: McLaren boss Andrea Stella lays down the law after “unacceptable” F1 Sprint clash
Andrea Stella demands unity after an unacceptable Sprint clash between Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri in Singapore
For McLaren fans. Papaya news from Woking, with the latest on the drivers, the car, team strategy and every race weekend.

The 2026 Singapore Grand Prix provided a stark reality check for McLaren. While Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri ultimately secured a double-points finish in Sunday's main event, the weekend was heavily overshadowed by a disastrous inter-team collision during Saturday's Sprint race and a glaring pace deficit to their championship rivals.

Following the chequered flag, McLaren team principal Andrea Stella addressed both the car's current performance ceiling and the internal garage dynamics, making it explicitly clear that selfish driving will not be tolerated as the team fights for its position in the Constructors' Championship.

The boiling point of McLaren's weekend occurred during the final lap of the wet-weather Sprint race. While hunting down Ferrari's Charles Leclerc, Norris executed an aggressive lunge down the inside of Piastri at Turn 5. The two Papaya cars made heavy contact, sending Piastri into the wall for a DNF while Norris limped home in eighth place, costing the team a massive haul of championship points.
Stella immediately convened a meeting with both drivers, demanding a complete reset of their racing rules of engagement.

"As for what happened yesterday in the Sprint race, I said that it was an unacceptable incident, and I was very pleased that our drivers also took this view," Stella revealed following Sunday's Grand Prix. "So, we’re on the same page about how we want to move this team forward, in a joint effort."
Lando Norris, McLaren, Oscar Piastri, McLaren
Rather than assigning explicit blame for the Turn 5 contact, the McLaren boss used the disaster to reinforce the squad's core operational philosophy.

"We’ll discuss it further, but not because we need to revisit the ‘why’ or ‘how’ of the contact, but to reflect together on what sort of team we want to be," Stella stated firmly. "We must be aware that, whether we’re at the factory, in the pitlane or in the cockpit of a car, the team’s interests take precedence over any individual’s interests."
Norris eventually apologised for the incident over the team radio, a gesture Stella expects to become the standard moving forward.

"This is what I, and everyone who works at McLaren Mastercard, expect from our drivers," Stella added. "I was therefore pleased with what Lando said during the final laps of the race, and I expect to see more examples of this in the future."
Beyond the internal garage politics, Stella openly acknowledged that the MCL40 currently lacks the raw aerodynamic performance to consistently challenge Red Bull and Ferrari for race victories.

"All in all, today’s result reflects the current level of performance of our car: it’s no coincidence that it’s very similar to what we saw yesterday in Qualifying," Stella admitted. "Perhaps there was a chance for Lando to take third place, but after a challenging Saturday and a few races where we didn’t get the results we’d hoped for, picking up these points is a small consolation."
Oscar Piastri, McLaren, Lando Norris, McLaren
However, with a critical triple-header approaching—featuring races in Austin, Mexico, and Brazil—Stella confirmed that Woking is preparing a major development package to reignite its season.

"It gives us confidence as we prepare for the next trio of races and focus on introducing updates that, we hope, will enable us to fight for the podium," Stella concluded. "We know that although Red Bull have taken a step forward, this result confirms that we are right in the thick of the battle with our current main rivals in the championship and that the gap to the frontrunners is one we believe we can close."
